patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — BigCommerce and Webflow share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose BigCommerce only if your buying job matches “Open-SaaS ecommerce platform — Core $39/mo ($29 annual), Growth $105 ($79), Scale $399 ($2” rather than Webflow's shape. Choose Webflow only if your buying job matches “Design-led website platform with Ecommerce — Standard $29/mo (500 items, 2% fee), Plus $74” rather than BigCommerce's shape. Workflow advantage: BigCommerce leans catalog-management, wholesale-b2b; Webflow leans website-builder-commerce. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — BigCommerce and Webflow share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: BigCommerce is Open-SaaS ecommerce platform — Core $39/mo ($29 annual), Growth $105 ($79), Scale $399 ($299); GMV thresholds and open payment provider fees; Webflow is Design-led website platform with Ecommerce — Standard $29/mo (500 items, 2% fee), Plus $74 highlighted (5,000 items, 0% fee), Advanced $212 .
- Company-size focus: BigCommerce (small-business, mid-market, enterprise) vs Webflow (solo, micro, small-business).
- Workflow coverage skew: BigCommerce-leaning catalog-management, wholesale-b2b vs Webflow-leaning website-builder-commerce.
- Researched limits: BigCommerce — 2026 GMV thresholds and open payment provider fees complicate TCO versus headline subscription; Webflow — Ecommerce requires a Site plan in addition to the Ecommerce plan — model combined TCO, not the $29 floor alone.

Limitations — BigCommerce: 2026 GMV thresholds and open payment provider fees complicate TCO versus headline subscription; Native POS/retail depth trails Shopify/Square for omnichannel-first merchants; Webflow: Ecommerce requires a Site plan in addition to the Ecommerce plan — model combined TCO, not the $29 floor alone; Catalog caps (500 / 5,000 / 15,000 items) and Standard’s 2% transaction fee trail Shopify-class commerce OS depth.

Poor-fit cases: BigCommerce is a poor fit when that limitation bites: 2026 GMV thresholds and open payment provider fees complicate TCO versus headline subscription · Webflow is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Ecommerce requires a Site plan in addition to the Ecommerce plan — model combined TCO, not the $29 floor alone · Avoid BigCommerce if you actually need Webflow's motion (Design-led website platform with Ecommerce — Standard $29/mo (500 items, 2% fee))

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
